source_work: Noah Webster, An American Dictionary of the English Language (1828)
rights_basis: The original 1828 dictionary text is public domain; only its historical definitions and examples are transcribed, not website editorial material.
transcription_source: Internet Archive volume 2 printed page scans and OCR, cross-checked against clean online Webster transcriptions; original OCR is retained unchanged.
selection_method: Selected the next four exact KJV-used S headwords in alphabetical order from the unreviewed high/medium OCR queue. This is a targeted OCR queue, not a claim that all Webster entries have been reviewed.
review_method: Visually checked every sense against the printed page scans and used clean online transcriptions only as secondary aids. Corrected OCR substitutions, scan breaks, page headers, punctuation, and numbering; retained historical examples, usage labels, and author citations. Expanded parts of speech and normalized whitespace for display. Source spans are one-based lines in the hash-verified OCR file.
review_scope: All definitions and examples: the SPITE noun definition, usage discussion, phrases, and three transitive senses; ten STATION noun senses and its transitive definition; three STEALTH noun senses; five STEM noun senses and two transitive senses. Readable etymology is retained for SPITE, STATION, and STEM. The scan's simple STEALTH pronunciation form is retained without inventing an etymology.

entries.review_note: Scans n640-n641 confirm the noun discussion, both in spite of examples, to owe one a spite, three transitive senses, Darius, and the Not used label. Removed the SPL running header and did not merge SPITED.

Scan n660 confirms the readable etymology, ten noun senses, and transitive definition. It resolves performed, spending the sabbath, its station, importance, and military where the base OCR or online transcription is damaged. Excluded STATIONAL and following entries.
Scan n662 confirms all three senses, stelth, Spenser, Raleigh, Pope, and Dryden citations, and used in a good or bad sense. Removed STE column contamination and excluded STEALTHY.

Scan n664 confirms the readable etymology, five noun senses, two transitive senses, Tickel, scarfed, stem to stern, Denham, and Pope. This corrects the base OCR's plant, bough, they, stem to stem, and quotation damage; excluded STEM-CLASPING and later entries.
